security_audit.summary: All 41 static findings are false positives caused by template literals, fixed local requests, relative module paths, SQL, and documentation links. The examples expose unauthenticated deployment routes that create deployments under caller-selected identifiers, creating resource-abuse risk outside local development. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Example deployment routes accept unauthenticated POST requests and caller-selected application identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Add authentication, authorization, identifier validation, and rate limits before adapting these routes for shared or production environments.

content.value_statement: Building a generated backend for each user requires deployment, routing, durable state, and lifecycle patterns. This skill provides Rivet documentation links and runnable TypeScript examples.
actual_capabilities: Locates Rivet guidance for authentication, deployment, routing, realtime behavior, background work, and state.
Demonstrates deployment of generated in-memory application files with deployApp.
Shows HTTP routing for deployed applications through a Hono host server.
Provides RivetKit actor examples for shared multiplayer state and typed clients.
Demonstrates parameterized SQLite storage for persistent actor notes.
Shows a durable workflow with named steps, state transitions, and a delay.
limitations: Examples target local development and omit production access controls around deployment routes.
The skill depends on external Rivet documentation for detailed platform behavior.
It does not provision cloud infrastructure or configure a production Rivet environment.
Generated applications still require security review, testing, monitoring, and resource limits.

use_cases.title: Prototype Generated Backends
use_cases.description: Create a local service that deploys a separate generated HTTP backend for each user or project.

use_cases.title: Add Durable Application State
use_cases.description: Select actor, SQLite, workflow, or realtime patterns for generated applications that require persistent coordination.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Rivet Architecture
use_cases.description: Review runnable patterns before adopting Rivet Dynamic Apps for a multi-tenant product.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Basic Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a local Rivet Dynamic App that serves an HTML page and one JSON endpoint. Explain how to run and deploy it.

prompt_templates.title: Add Persistent Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RivetKit notes actor with parameterized SQLite operations. Include deployment flow, typed client usage, validation, and local test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Shared Realtime State
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a multiplayer room actor for named players and positions. Include broadcasts, typed client calls, authorization boundaries, and cleanup behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Deployment Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Architect a multi-tenant Dynamic Apps deployment API. Cover authentication, authorization, identifier validation, isolation, quotas, observability, rollback, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Build a generated hello-world backend with one API endpoint.
output_examples.output: A deployment plan with generated files, a host router, local run commands, an application URL, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Add persistent shared notes to a Dynamic App.
output_examples.output: A RivetKit actor design using parameterized SQLite statements, typed client actions, migration guidance, input validation, and persistence tests.

output_examples.input: Prepare the deployment example for a shared staging environment.
output: Require authenticated deployment requests and authorize each application identifier.
Validate identifiers, restrict source inputs, and enforce quotas.
Add audit logs, health checks, rollback procedures, and isolated namespaces.

best_practices: Start with a checked local fixture before accepting generated application files.
Authenticate deployment routes and isolate each tenant with validated identifiers, namespaces, and resource quotas.
Use parameterized database operations and test deployment, routing, persistence, cleanup, and failure recovery.
anti_patterns: Do not expose example deployment routes to shared networks without authentication and rate limits.
Do not allow unvalidated request values to select filesystem sources, package inputs, or tenant namespaces.
Do not treat generated backend code as trusted without review, sandboxing, dependency controls, and monitoring.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build generated Rivet backends with HTTP routes, actors, SQLite state, workflows, and multiplayer coordination.

faq.question: Does the skill deploy production infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation links and local examples, but production provisioning and operations remain your responsibility.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are the deployment endpoints production ready?
faq.answer: No. Add authentication, authorization, validation, isolation, quotas, and rate limits before shared use.

faq.question: Does it include persistent data examples?
faq.answer: Yes. The SQLite example stores notes through parameterized RivetKit database operations.

faq.question: Does it cover durable background work?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow example demonstrates named steps, state transitions, and a durable delay.
